A.title: Misao Oguri (小栗操): The Rename-and-Return Into a Triple Exclusive
A.body: --- title: 'Misao Oguri (小栗操): The Rename-and-Return Into a Triple Exclusive' description: 'Japanese AV actress Misao Oguri — debuted 2020 as "Asuka Momose," announced retirement in 2023, then returned in May 2025 under the name Misao Oguri as a triple exclusive at Honnaka, Das and ROYAL. The retirement that was a reset, not an end.' pubDate: 'Aug 10 2026' updatedDate: 'Aug 10 2026' heroImage: '../../assets/portraits/momose-asuka.jpg' tags: ['Misao Oguri', 'Asuka Momose', 'AV Actress', 'JAV', 'Adult Film', 'Comeback'] category: 'JAV Actresses' keyword: 'misao oguri av actress' faq: - question: 'Who is Misao Oguri?' answer: 'A Japanese AV actress who debuted in 2020 as "Asuka Momose" and returned in May 2025 under the name Misao Oguri. Her stage name changed; the career restarted.' - question: 'When did she debut?' answer: 'In September 2020, as Asuka Momose, on SOD Creative''s "Youth Era" label. Before that she had trained in voice acting and done TV-commercial narration.' - question: 'Did she retire?' answer: 'She announced retirement on 18 February 2023, effective 31 December 2023, and deleted her account. She restarted social media in March 2023, then announced the return on 20 May 2025.' - question: 'How did she return?' answer: 'As Misao Oguri, a triple exclusive at Honnaka, Das and ROYAL, under the agency Jun Pro. She went freelance again in July 2026.' - question: 'What has she achieved?' answer: 'Repeated FANZA campaign-girl appointments in 2021–2022, including the Triple Happy Campaign twice.' --- import { Image } from 'astro:assets'; import momoseAsukaPortrait from '../../assets/portraits/momose-asuka.jpg'; Misao Oguri's career is the retirement-as-reset case. **Debuted 2020 as Asuka Momose, announced retirement in February 2023, deleted her account — then returned in May 2025 under a new name as a triple exclusive at Honnaka, Das and ROYAL.** The name change was the point: it was not a comeback, it was a restart. ## The short version | | | |---|---| | **Name** | Misao Oguri (小栗操) · formerly Asuka Momose (百瀬あすか) | | **Born** | 31 May 2000, Tokyo | | **Debut** | September 2020, SOD "Youth Era", as Asuka Momose | | **Retired** | Announced Feb 2023, effective Dec 2023 | | **Return** | May 2025, as Misao Oguri, triple exclusive | | **Now** | Freelance (from July 2026) | ## 2020–2023: Asuka Momose She debuted in **September 2020** as **Asuka Momose** on SOD's "Youth Era" label. Her background was unusual: raised through a girls'-school track, she had trained at a **voice-acting agency** through part of college and done TV-commercial narration. She went freelance in 2021 and held repeated campaign-girl posts (Triple Happy Campaign 2021 and 2022, Sweet Campaign and Golden Week Campaign 2022). On **18 February 2023** she announced retirement effective **31 December 2023**, and deleted her account the same day. ## 2025: the return as Misao Oguri On **20 May 2025** she announced the return under **Misao Oguri**, as a **triple exclusive at Honnaka, Das and ROYAL**, under the agency Jun Pro. In **July 2026** she went freelance again. The return's scale — triple exclusivity, not a quiet re-entry — is what makes the retirement read as a reset rather than an end. She left, restarted under a new name, and was immediately placed at the industry's top contract tier. ## What this career means **The retirement that was a rebrand.** Oguri's arc shows the industry's "retirement" mechanism being used as a reset point: she stopped as Asuka Momose and restarted as Misao Oguri, at a higher contract level. Alongside [Azu Amatsuki's two-name arc](/blog/amatsuki-azu/), it documents that the name is not fixed and the stop is not final. [Retirement stops new production](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/); it does not prevent it from starting again. ## Related reading - [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — retirement and return - [Azu Amatsuki](/blog/amatsuki-azu/) — the other rename-and-return - [Saito Amiri](/blog/saito-amiri/) — the limited comeback - [How Japan's adult video industry works](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) — Honnaka, Das and Hokuto **Sources:** [Japanese Wikipedia — 小栗操](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/小栗操). Career facts only; nothing here is sourced from fan wikis or aggregator biographies. **Photo:** [Wikimedia Commons「File:Fresh Festival 2023 in Shirakobato Water Park IMG 1268.jpg」](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Fresh_Festival_2023_in_Shirakobato_Water_Park_IMG_1268.jpg) (CC BY-SA 4.0, photo by Bject). Used on the cover and in the article.

B.title: Tsukasa Aoi (葵つかさ): The 15-Year Exclusive Career That Ended on Schedule
B.body: --- title: 'Tsukasa Aoi (葵つかさ): The 15-Year Exclusive Career That Ended on Schedule' description: 'From gravure in 2008 to an Alice Japan debut in 2010 and S1 in 2015 — then a quiet Instagram retirement in July 2025, effective 17 August. Over 700 titles across two labels, never dropping out of the exclusive tier.' pubDate: 'Aug 10 2026' updatedDate: 'Aug 10 2026' heroImage: '../../assets/portraits/tsukasa-aoi.jpg' tags: ['Tsukasa Aoi', 'AV Actress', 'JAV', 'Adult Film', 'Retirement'] category: 'JAV Actresses' keyword: 'tsukasa aoi' faq: - question: 'When did Tsukasa Aoi debut in AV?' answer: 'She debuted as a gravure model in October 2008, then made her AV debut on 8 October 2010 with Alice Japan in Absolute Girl Aoi Tsukasa. She was born on 14 August 1990 in Osaka.' - question: 'Which studios did she work for?' answer: 'Alice Japan from her 2010 debut until 2015, then S1 No. 1 Style from 2015. Her last Alice Japan title was released on 22 May 2015. She stayed exclusive for the entire career, across more than 700 titles.' - question: 'What "firsts" did she achieve as an active AV actress?' answer: 'In February 2011 she became the first active AV actress to appear on a magazine cover (Saizo). In 2013 she appeared in the Taiwanese drama True Love 365, reported as the first AV actress to appear in a Taiwanese drama.' - question: 'When did she retire?' answer: 'She announced her retirement on Instagram on 20 July 2025, effective 17 August 2025 — roughly 15 years after her gravure debut.' - question: 'What awards did she win?' answer: 'The FLASH Award at the 2012 Adult Broadcasting Awards, and the Special Presenter Award at the 2016 DMM Adult Awards. She was nominated for Best Actress at the 2019 FANZA Adult Awards.' --- import { Image } from 'astro:assets'; import tsukasaAoiPortrait from '../../assets/portraits/tsukasa-aoi.jpg'; Careers in this industry are short, and even the exclusive ones end when a term is not renewed. **Tsukasa Aoi is the exception that ran the whole distance: gravure in 2008, AV in 2010, and a retirement announced in July 2025, effective 17 August — fifteen years spent inside the exclusive tier and nowhere else.** Over **700 titles**, two labels, and a set of "firsts" she accumulated while still active. This is the profile of the career that did not fall. ## The short version | | | |---|---| | **Name** | Tsukasa Aoi (葵つかさ) | | **Born** | 14 August 1990, Osaka | | **Gravure debut** | October 2008, Bejean magazine | | **AV debut** | 8 October 2010, Alice Japan | | **Main labels** | Alice Japan (2010–2015) → S1 No. 1 Style (2015–) | | **Titles** | 700+ | | **Awards** | FLASH Award 2012; Special Presenter Award 2016 | | **Retired** | 17 August 2025 (announced 20 July 2025) | ## 2008: gravure first She entered through the industry's most common doorway: gravure. In **October 2008** she debuted in a uniform gravure feature in *Bejean* magazine, then worked on regional television in Kansai — Sun Television and Television Osaka shows. Gravure sits next door to adult video in this industry, which is precisely why the step is so common. [Our careers explainer](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) lists it as one of the three standard routes in. ## 2010: the Alice Japan debut She made her AV debut on **8 October 2010** with Alice Japan, in *Absolute Girl Aoi Tsukasa*, as an exclusive. That placement matters: Alice Japan's exclusivity is the "sold by name" tier, the opposite of the freelance work-for-hire route. In **February 2011** she appeared on the cover of *Saizo* magazine — reported as **the first active AV actress ever to grace a magazine cover**. The firsts were coming before the career was a year old. ## Film and Taiwan: the crossovers The mainstream work ran alongside the AV career. - **2012** — she starred in *Female Prisoner No. 701 – Sasori*, Ken'ichi Fujiwara's remake of the 1972 *Female Convict 701: Scorpion* — a leading role in a mainstream film. - **2013** — a guest appearance in the Taiwanese drama *True Love 365*, reported as **the first AV actress to appear in a Taiwanese drama**. - **2014** — she featured as a Sailor Moon AV model in *Naked Ambition 2*, and appeared in *A Record of Sweet Murder*. The Taiwan connection matters beyond the curiosity of it. It is the same East Asian reception that made [Yui Hatano's transit-card incident](/blog/yui-hatano/) a national story — the industry's performers treated as public figures rather than marginalised ones. ## 2015: Alice Japan to S1 In **2015** she transferred from Alice Japan to **S1 No. 1 Style**, the flagship label of the [Hokuto Corporation group](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/). Her last Alice Japan title was released on **22 May 2015**. That same year, on **26 September 2015**, she joined the second-generation **Ebisu Muscats** — the same generation as [Yua Mikami](/blog/yua-mikami/). She graduated in June 2018. The awards clustered around this period: the **FLASH Award** at the 2012 Adult Broadcasting Awards, the **Special Presenter Award** at the 2016 DMM Adult Awards, and a Best Actress nomination at the 2019 FANZA Adult Awards. ## 2025: the retirement on schedule On **20 July 2025** she announced on Instagram that she would retire on **17 August 2025**. Fifteen years after the gravure debut, the career closed on the date she chose. Retirement means new production stops, and nothing else. It does not withdraw the existing catalogue — that was never what *intai* did. The [2022 performer-protection law's cancellation right](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) applies to titles released within one year (two under transitional provisions); the overwhelming majority of her 700-plus titles predate it entirely. Her final years' work falls under the new law; the rest does not. Both facts are normal. ## What the career means **The exclusive tier, run to its full length.** The ordinary outcome in this industry is a term that ends without renewal, and a career that leaves almost no public record. Aoi's is the documented opposite: fifteen years, two labels, no fall to the freelance tier, and a retirement she announced herself rather than one that happened to her. Against the other profiles on this site, she is the closest thing to the "career as advertised" — the promoted exclusive who stayed promoted until she decided to stop. That is precisely why she is worth profiling: in this industry, it is the rarest outcome of all. ## Related reading - [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the exclusive tier and retirement - [Yua Mikami](/blog/yua-mikami/) — the same Ebisu Muscats generation - [Yui Hatano](/blog/yui-hatano/) — the long career and East Asian fame - [How Japan's adult video industry works](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) — S1, Hokuto, and the 2022 law **Sources:** [English Wikipedia — Tsukasa Aoi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsukasa_Aoi). Career facts only; nothing here is sourced from fan wikis or aggregator biographies. **Photo:** [Wikimedia Commons「File:아오이츠카사(Aoi Tsukasa) 국내 팬미팅 5.jpg」](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:%EC%95%84%EC%98%A4%EC%9D%B4%EC%B8%A0%EC%B9%B4%EC%82%AC(Aoi_Tsukasa)_%EA%B5%AD%EB%82%B4_%ED%8C%AC%EB%AF%B8%ED%8C%85_5.jpg) (CC BY 4.0, photo by SJ). Used on the cover and in the article.

A.title: Sora Aoi (蒼井そら): The Career That Proved the Crossover Was Possible
A.body: --- title: 'Sora Aoi (蒼井そら): The Career That Proved the Crossover Was Possible' description: 'Debut in 2002, retirement in 2011, 600-plus titles — and then 13 million followers in China. A career profile of the first Japanese adult performer to become a mainstream East Asian celebrity.' pubDate: 'Jul 30 2026' updatedDate: 'Aug 04 2026' heroImage: '../../assets/portraits/sora-aoi.jpg' tags: ['Sora Aoi', 'AV Actress', 'JAV', 'Adult Film', 'Japan'] category: 'JAV Actresses' keyword: 'sora aoi' faq: - question: 'When did Sora Aoi debut and retire?' answer: 'She debuted in July 2002 with a title for Alice Japan and effectively retired from adult video in 2011, her last original release appearing on 7 June 2011. She appeared in more than 600 titles across those nine years.' - question: 'Why is Sora Aoi so famous in China?' answer: 'She opened a Sina Weibo account in November 2010 and gained roughly 130,000 followers within the first six hours. By September 2012 the account had passed 13 million followers. She went on to release a Mandarin-language song and became one of the most widely recognised Japanese public figures in China.' - question: 'What did Sora Aoi do after retiring?' answer: 'She had already been working in mainstream media since 2003 — Japanese dramas, films, variety television and a 2006 music album. After 2011 she continued acting in domestic and international productions, and has since worked in brand ambassadorship and collaborations, including a 2022 music video with Malaysian artist Namewee.' - question: 'Is Sora Aoi still active?' answer: 'Not in adult video, which she left in 2011. She has remained publicly active in media, brand and social-media work in the years since, and married and started a family in 2018–2019, both of which she announced publicly.' - question: 'What was Sora Aoi’s first film?' answer: 'Happy Go Lucky!, released in July 2002 by Alice Japan.' --- import { Image } from 'astro:assets'; import soraAoiPortrait from '../../assets/portraits/sora-aoi.jpg'; Ask why anyone writes profiles of adult performers at all and Sora Aoi is the answer. Her career is the one that demonstrated the ceiling was not where everybody assumed it was — and she did it before social media, before subtitles, and before the industry had any interest in an audience outside Japan. This is a career profile. Work, dates, and what is actually on the public record. ## The short version | | | |---|---| | **Name** | Sora Aoi (蒼井そら) | | **Debut** | July 2002 — *Happy Go Lucky!*, Alice Japan | | **Retired from AV** | 2011; last original release 7 June 2011 | | **Titles** | 600+ | | **Best known for** | Mainstream crossover; enormous following in China | | **Status** | Retired from adult video; active in media and brand work | ## 2002: the debut She debuted in **July 2002** with *Happy Go Lucky!* for **Alice Japan**, one of the established labels of the period. Context matters for reading what followed. This is pre-streaming, pre-FANZA, pre-anything resembling an international distribution route. The industry was a DVD business selling to a domestic market, and a performer's reach was bounded by what a rental shop in Japan would stock. Nobody was building an overseas audience because there was no mechanism to build one with. Over the next nine years she appeared in more than **600 titles** — volume that puts her in the high-output bracket rather than the boutique exclusive tier, which is worth noting given what her name later came to signify. ## 2003 onward: the mainstream work started early The thing most people get wrong about her is the sequence. The mainstream career did not begin after she retired. **It began in 2003**, one year in, and ran alongside everything else. Television appearances from 2003. Roles in Japanese dramas and theatrical films. A music album, *Hadaka no Kiss*, in **2006**. Variety show work, guest slots, the ordinary furniture of a Japanese media career — accumulated while she was still an active performer. That simultaneity is the actually unusual part, and it is what makes her career a template rather than an anecdote. She was not someone who left the industry and rebuilt. She was someone who ran both tracks at once for the better part of a decade. ## November 2010: China Then the part nobody, including her, could have planned. She opened a **Sina Weibo** account in **November 2010**. It picked up roughly **130,000 followers in the first six hours**. By **September 2012** it had passed **13 million**. Read those numbers against the fact that her actual work was, and is, illegal to distribute in China. The audience had found her through channels nobody controlled and no company monetised. She was, by a wide margin, one of the most recognised Japanese public figures in the country — a position no Japanese studio's marketing department had built, budgeted for, or could replicate. She leaned into it rather than away: a Mandarin-language single, appearances, sustained engagement with a Chinese-language audience. Whatever else is true, this was a person who understood what had happened to her faster than the industry around her did. ## 2011: retirement, and what it did not mean Her last original release came on **7 June 2011**, closing the adult-video chapter after nine years. Worth being precise about what that changed, because English coverage routinely misreads it. Retirement stopped new production. It did not withdraw 600 existing titles from circulation, and at the time no mechanism existed to do so — [Japan's statutory right to cancel a release](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) did not arrive until 2022, eleven years later. Every performer who retired before then retired into exactly the situation she did: no new work, all the old work, permanently. ## Since Acting work in domestic and international productions continued through 2015. Brand ambassadorship, including a global brand role in 2022/23, and a collaboration on a music video with Malaysian artist **Namewee** in December 2022. She married in **January 2018** and had twin sons in **May 2019**, both announced publicly by her. ## Why this career is the reference case Three reasons it gets cited more than any other. **It proved the ceiling was wrong.** The assumption inside the industry was that adult work closed the door on mainstream media permanently. She ran both simultaneously for nine years and then continued for another decade. That is not a loophole; it is a counterexample. **It happened without infrastructure.** No subtitles, no international storefront, no social platform designed to carry her. The Weibo numbers were not built by a strategy — they were the visible surface of an audience that already existed and that nobody had noticed. **It reframed the East Asian picture.** The gap between how Japanese adult performers are treated inside Japan and how they are received across the rest of the region is not small, and hers was the career that made it impossible to ignore. [Yui Hatano's Taiwan transit-card episode in 2015](/blog/yui-hatano/) is the same phenomenon in a more concentrated form. The caveat, which we would attach to any profile: this is an **outlier career**, documented precisely because it was exceptional. The ordinary version of this job produces almost no public record at all, which is the point we make at length in [the actresses overview](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/). ## Related reading - [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the structural picture - [Yui Hatano](/blog/yui-hatano/) — the long career, and the same East Asian phenomenon - [Yua Mikami](/blog/yua-mikami/) — idol to industry and back out again - [How Japan's adult video industry works](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) — labels, contracts, the 2022 law **Sources:** [English Wikipedia — Sola Aoi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sola_Aoi). Career facts only; nothing here is sourced from fan wikis or aggregator biographies.

B.title: Momonga Kana (桃乃木かな): Ten Years as an IdeaPocket Exclusive, Ending on Her Own Terms
B.body:
---
title: 'Momonga Kana (桃乃木かな): Ten Years as an IdeaPocket Exclusive, Ending on Her Own Terms'
description: 'Japanese AV actress Momonga Kana — IdeaPocket exclusive from October 2015 to her November 2025 retirement, no label changes in ten years. New Actress awards in 2017, the industry''s first Ultra HD Blu-ray lead in 2021, and a retirement announced in September 2025.'
pubDate: 'Aug 10 2026'
updatedDate: 'Aug 10 2026'
heroImage: '../../assets/heroes/momonogi-kana.webp'
tags: ['Momonga Kana', 'AV Actress', 'JAV', 'Adult Film', 'Retirement']
category: 'JAV Actresses'
keyword: 'momonga kana av actress'
altJa: 'https://ja.chon-mage.com/blog/momonogi-kana/'
faq:
  - question: 'When did Momonga Kana debut in AV?'
    answer: 'On 19 October 2015, as an IdeaPocket exclusive, in the FIRST IMPRESSION series.'
  - question: 'Which studios did she work for?'
    answer: 'Only IdeaPocket. She was exclusive there from debut to retirement, no label changes, across more than 100 titles.'
  - question: 'What did she achieve?'
    answer: 'New Actress and Tokyo Sports awards at the 2017 Sky PerfecTV! ceremony, the DMM Media Award in 2017, and the industry''s first Ultra HD Blu-ray lead in January 2021.'
  - question: 'When did she retire?'
    answer: 'She announced on 28 September 2025 that she would retire with her 7 October 2025 release. Her final title, -FINAL IMPRESSION-, released 11 November 2025, plus an 8K VR final.'
  - question: 'What is she doing now?'
    answer: 'She continues as a celebrity and singer, with a Taiwan photo session and web variety appearances in 2026, and has talked about running a restaurant.'
---

import SnsEmbed from '../../components/SnsEmbed.astro';

Momonga Kana is the exclusive-tier career at its cleanest. **IdeaPocket from October 2015 to November 2025 — ten years, no label changes, more than 100 titles — ended with a retirement she announced and dated herself.** In an industry where the ordinary exclusive career ends when a contract quietly is not renewed, hers ended on a schedule she set.

## The short version

| | |
|---|---|
| **Name** | Momonga Kana (桃乃木かな) |
| **Born** | 24 December 1996, Tokyo |
| **Debut** | 19 October 2015, IdeaPocket |
| **Label** | IdeaPocket exclusive, 2015–2025 |
| **Titles** | 100+ (100th in May 2024) |
| **Awards** | New Actress + Tokyo Sports 2017; DMM Media Award 2017 |
| **Retired** | November 2025 (announced 28 September 2025) |

## 2015: the scouted debut

She was scouted in Ikebukuro in 2015 and debuted on **19 October 2015** as an IdeaPocket exclusive, in the FIRST IMPRESSION line. The label placement mattered: IdeaPocket is the [Hokuto group's](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) flagship for promoted, named exclusives. She stayed there for the entire decade.

## 2017: the awards

- **March 2017** — New Actress and Tokyo Sports awards, Sky PerfecTV! ceremony
- **2017** — DMM Media Award

That same period she joined the second-generation **Ebisu Muscats** in September 2015, staying until the group's effective dissolution in August 2022.

## 2021: the industry-first Ultra HD Blu-ray

In **January 2021** she starred in the industry's **first Ultra HD Blu-ray release** — a three-studio simultaneous title (IdeaPocket, Premium, Das). The 4K format lead was a genuine industry milestone, and it went to a ten-year exclusive, which is itself the point: the format's debut went to the established name, not a newcomer.

## 2024: the 100th title

Her **100th title** released in May 2024, an 8th-anniversary marker. Ten years and 100 titles, all IdeaPocket, all exclusive.

## 2025: the retirement on schedule

On **28 September 2025** she announced she would retire with her **7 October 2025** release. Her final titles were **-FINAL IMPRESSION- IdeaPocket Legend Momonga Kana, Retires** on **11 November 2025**, and an 8K VR title on **21 November 2025**. Ten years, closed on her own date.

Retirement ends new production and nothing else. Her existing catalogue remains in circulation, as it does for every retiree — [the 2022 law's cancellation right](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) applies to recent titles only, and most of her work predates it.

Her own X account still documents the post-retirement activity, including a Macau event announcement for September 2026.

<SnsEmbed
	kind="x"
	url="https://x.com/Kana_Momonogi/status/2084562834235830611"
	label="Momonga Kana (@Kana_Momonogi) on X — a Macau event, 2026"
/>

## What this career means

**The exclusive career, run to its term, ending on her schedule.** Against [Otsuki's freelance volume](/blog/hibiki-otsuki/) and [Matsumoto's tier-hopping](/blog/matsumoto-ichika/), Momonga Kana is the straight-line exclusive: one label, ten years, 100 titles, and a retirement she announced, dated and kept. The "IdeaPocket legend" framing of her final title was not marketing; it was the accurate summary of the shape.

## Related reading

- [Tsukasa Aoi](/blog/tsukasa-aoi/) — the other fifteen-year exclusive
- [Akiho Yoshizawa](/blog/akiho-yoshizawa/) — the other long exclusive

The award record matched it: **Best New Actress at the Weekly Playboy Adult Awards 2021**, **#1 in the FANZA monthly ranking in September 2021**, and **#3 in the FANZA H1 2022 ranking**. ## 2025: the deliberate step back On **27 May 2025** she announced she was leaving exclusivity. From **June 2025** she returned to the **freelance tier**, after roughly four years as a contracted exclusive. This is the uncommon direction — [exclusive to freelance is usually the end](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/), not a pivot. For Kitano it was a choice: she immediately resumed heavy output across h.m.p, Glory Quest, MOODYZ, Das, Max-A and Madonna, and in **H2 2025 ranked #10 in FANZA, #4 among freelance performers**. ## Now As of 2026 she is active in the freelance tier, releasing several titles a month, with 2025 her heaviest year at roughly 77 DVD titles. Her X account documents the day-to-day. ## What this career means **Both tiers, at maximum, in sequence — and the return direction works.** Kitano proved the exclusive tier could promote her to four studios, then proved the freelance tier could still rank her top ten after she walked away from the contracts. It is the mirror image of [Ichika Matsumoto](/blog/matsumoto-ichika/), who went freelance → exclusive; Kitano went exclusive → freelance, and both ended in the top ten. ## Related reading - [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the two tiers - [Ichika Matsumoto](/blog/matsumoto-ichika/) — the freelance-to-exclusive mirror image - [Waka Misono](/blog/misono-waka/) — another tier-switching record-breaker - [How Japan's adult video industry works](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) — MOODYZ, Das and Hokuto **Sources:** [Japanese Wikipedia — 北野未奈](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/北野未奈). Career facts only; nothing here is sourced from fan wikis or aggregator biographies. **Photo:** [Wikimedia Commons「File:Midsummer Swimsuit Festival (July 3, 2025)DSC 6789.jpg」](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Midsummer_Swimsuit_Festival_(July_3,_2025)DSC_6789.jpg) (CC BY 4.0, photo by Bject). Used on the cover and in the article.

B.title: Kirara Asuka (明日花キララ): AV Actress, Beauty Brand, and the Retirement Into Modelling
B.body: --- title: 'Kirara Asuka (明日花キララ): AV Actress, Beauty Brand, and the Retirement Into Modelling' description: 'AV actress Kirara Asuka — scouted at a Roppongi hostess bar, debuted on h.m.p in 2007, Best Actress 2009, S1 from 2013, retired 2020 into modelling. Her career and post-2020 work, documented on the public record.' pubDate: 'Aug 10 2026' updatedDate: 'Aug 10 2026' heroImage: '../../assets/portraits/kirara-asuka.jpg' tags: ['Kirara Asuka', 'AV Actress', 'JAV', 'Adult Film', 'Retirement'] category: 'JAV Actresses' keyword: 'kirara asuka' faq: - question: 'When did Kirara Asuka debut in AV?' answer: 'On 21 December 2007, with h.m.p in Miracle Beautiful Breasts. Before that she worked as a waitress at a hostess bar in Roppongi, where an AV company scout approached her on the spot.' - question: 'Which studios did she work for?' answer: 'h.m.p from 2007 to 2009, Prestige from October 2009 to April 2013 (42 titles), then S1 No. 1 Style from June 2013.' - question: 'What awards did she win?' answer: 'Best Actress at the 2009 Sky PerfecTV! Adult Broadcasting Awards, and the Talk of the Town Award at the 2014 DMM Adult Awards, shared with Akiho Yoshizawa.' - question: 'When did she retire?' answer: 'She announced her retirement on 4 February 2020, after roughly two years of inactivity. In June 2020 she opened the YouTube channel "Kiraland."' - question: 'What does she do now?' answer: 'She works as a model and influencer. Her June 2019 style book sold out its limited edition immediately and its standard edition within a month, mainly to women in their twenties.' --- import { Image } from 'astro:assets'; import SnsEmbed from '../../components/SnsEmbed.astro'; import kiraraAsukaPortrait from '../../assets/portraits/kirara-asuka.jpg'; This career is the clearest example on this site of beauty operating as a standalone product. **Kirara Asuka was scouted at a Roppongi hostess bar, debuted on h.m.p in 2007, and built a career whose back half ran almost entirely on how she looked rather than what she released.** Her awards cluster in the early years; the later career ran on presence. Then she retired, and the beauty business continued. ## The short version | | | |---|---| | **Name** | Kirara Asuka (明日花キララ) | | **Born** | 2 October 1988, Tokyo | | **Debut** | 21 December 2007, h.m.p | | **Labels** | h.m.p → Prestige (2009–2013) → S1 No. 1 Style (2013–) | | **Awards** | Best Actress 2009; DMM Talk of the Town 2014 | | **Retired** | 4 February 2020 (announced) | | **Now** | Model and influencer; YouTube "Kiraland" | ## 2007: scouted at a hostess bar Her entry is one of the industry's most typical routes, with a specific twist. Before her debut she worked as a **waitress at a hostess bar in Roppongi** — the kind of venue [our hostess bar guide](/blog/hostess-bars-japan-guide/) covers — where a customer who turned out to be an AV company scout approached her on the spot. She debuted on **21 December 2007** with h.m.p in *Miracle Beautiful Breasts*. The "scouted from hospitality" route is common; being scouted while actually working in a [kyabakura](/blog/hostess-bars-japan-guide/) is the version that made the news. ## 2009: Best Actress, and the move to Prestige The first peak came early. In **2009** she won **Best Actress at the Sky PerfecTV! Adult Broadcasting Awards** — two years after debut. That September her contract with h.m.p ended, and in **October** she moved to **Prestige**, where she appeared in **42 titles** until **April 2013**. ## 2013: S1 In **June 2013** she transferred to **S1 No. 1 Style**, the flagship label of the [Hokuto group](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/), alongside [Tsukasa Aoi](/blog/tsukasa-aoi/) and [Yua Mikami](/blog/yua-mikami/). In **2014** she won the **Talk of the Town Award** at the DMM Adult Awards — for a collaboration with [Akiho Yoshizawa](/blog/akiho-yoshizawa/). ## Film, music, Muscats The mainstream work ran in parallel. - **Film:** *Vitamin Love* (V-Cinema, 2010), the SF action film *Iron Girl* (2012) and its sequel *Iron Girl ULTIMATE WEAPON* (2015). - **Music:** she launched "KiraKira Music Lovers" in 2012 and released three singles that year (venue-only), then the iTunes single "Aishiteru yo" in February 2016. - **Ebisu Muscats:** joined 24 September 2015, became **fourth-generation leader** on 21 December 2015, appeared on the TV Tokyo variety *Muscat Night* (2015–2017), and graduated on 17 April 2018. ## 2020: retirement, after two quiet years On **4 February 2020** she announced her retirement, after roughly two years of inactivity. Her agency moved to Kiratis in June 2020, and on **11 June 2020** she opened the YouTube channel **"Kiraland."** The retirement was into a pre-existing second career. Her **June 2019 style book** had already sold out its limited edition immediately and its standard edition within a month, to buyers mainly in their twenties. That is the whole thesis of the later career: she sold a look, not a filmography, and the look outlasted the filmography. Her own account documented the transition, including the Kiraland launch in 2020. In **October 2022** she appeared in the music video for Malaysian musician Namewee's "What I Love." ## What the career means Two things. First, **the awards front-loaded**. Best Actress in 2009, Talk of the Town in 2014 — and then no more. The back half of the career had no titles to hang the numbers on; it ran on presence. That is the rarest shape on this site, and the one that most directly contradicts the catalogue-driven version of this industry. Second, **the exit was into an existing business, not a new one**. [Mikami](/blog/yua-mikami/) built her brands after retiring; Asuka's style book had already sold out a year before she announced it. The beauty product was never the retirement plan — it was the actual career, running alongside. Against [Okita's withdrawal](/blog/anri-okita/) and [Asami's music exit](/blog/yuma-asami/), this is the one where the second career was already profitable. ## Related reading - [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the exclusive tier and the exit - [How Japan's adult video industry works](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) — S1 and Hokuto - [Yua Mikami](/blog/yua-mikami/) — another exit into consumer brands - [Akiho Yoshizawa](/blog/akiho-yoshizawa/) — the 2014 award collaboration **Sources:** [English Wikipedia — Kirara Asuka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirara_Asuka). Career facts only; nothing here is sourced from fan wikis or aggregator biographies. **Photo:** [Wikimedia Commons「File:171021 아스카 키라라 팬미팅 2부 (홍대 브이홀) 1 (1).jpg」](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:171021_%EC%95%84%EC%8A%A4%EC%B9%B4_%ED%82%A4%EB%9D%BC%EB%9D%BC_%ED%8C%AC%EB%AF%B8%ED%8C%85_2%EB%B6%80_(%ED%99%8D%EB%8C%80_%EB%B8%8C%EC%9D%B4%ED%99%80)_1_(1).jpg) (CC BY 4.0, photo by 찌노메라). Used on the cover and in the article.

A.title: Tsubasa Amami (天海つばさ): Fifteen Years as an IdeaPocket Exclusive, Now on Hiatus
A.body:

description: 'Japanese AV actress Tsubasa Amami — IdeaPocket exclusive since October 2009, fifteen years without leaving the exclusive tier, a singer on the side, and on hiatus since November 2024. The endurance exclusive of the modern era.'
pubDate: 'Aug 10 2026'

import SnsEmbed from '../../components/SnsEmbed.astro';

Tsubasa Amami is the modern era's endurance exclusive. **IdeaPocket exclusive from October 2009 for fifteen years, without ever dropping to the freelance tier, with a singing career on the side, and on hiatus since November 2024.** The career that ran the exclusive contract to its maximum length, then stopped on her own announcement.

## The short version

| | |
|---|---|
| **Name** | Tsubasa Amami (天海つばさ) |
| **Debut** | October 2009, IdeaPocket |
| **Label** | IdeaPocket exclusive, 2009–2024 |
| **Awards** | Asagei award 2011; AV OPEN Best Package 2017 |
| **Also** | Singer (VITCH VITCH, 2011) |
| **Status** | On hiatus since November 2024 |

## 2009: the IdeaPocket debut

She debuted in **October 2009** as an **IdeaPocket exclusive**, in the First Impression line. She has been exclusive to IdeaPocket for the entire career, with only occasional single titles and collaborations elsewhere — never a move to the freelance tier.

## 2011–2017: the awards and the singing

- **March 2011** — Asagei award, Sky PerfecTV! ceremony
- **December 2011** — singing debut in the unit **VITCH VITCH**, with solo singing work after
- **2017** — Best Package, AV OPEN 2017 (fan-vote division)

## The endurance

Fifteen years at one exclusive label is the industry's maximum: the same order as [Tsukasa Aoi's fifteen years](/blog/tsukasa-aoi/) and [Momonga Kana's ten](/blog/momonogi-kana/). Where [Aika Yumeno](/blog/yumeno-aika/) holds the S1 endurance record, Amami holds the equivalent at IdeaPocket.

## 2024: the 15th anniversary and the hiatus

On **1 October 2024** she marked her 15th anniversary, and in **November 2024** she announced she was taking a break. She has been on hiatus since.

<SnsEmbed
	kind="x"
	url="https://x.com/Amamitsubasa000/status/1871565884353073558"
	label="Tsubasa Amami (@Amamitsubasa000) on X"
/>

## What this career means

**The exclusive tier's endurance, at IdeaPocket.** Amami's fifteen years without a tier change is the rarest shape in the industry — [the ordinary exclusive career ends or falls](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/), and hers did neither for a decade and a half. The hiatus, announced on her own schedule after the 15th anniversary, is the same self-determined ending as [Momonga Kana's retirement](/blog/momonogi-kana/), with the difference that Amami's is framed as a break rather than a full stop.

## Related reading

- [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the exclusive tier
- [Momonga Kana](/blog/momonogi-kana/) — the other long IdeaPocket exclusive
- [Tsukasa Aoi](/blog/tsukasa-aoi/) — the fifteen-year S1/Alice Japan career
- [How Japan's adult video industry works](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) — IdeaPocket and Hokuto

**Sources:** [Japanese Wikipedia — 天海つばさ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/天海つばさ). Career facts only; nothing here is sourced from fan wikis or aggregator biographies.

Her entry was the archetype: she has said she did not think of herself as having a large bust until the industry interview pointed it out. ## 2022: freelance In **April 2022** she left exclusivity for the **freelance tier**, working across many studios including uncredited concept work. ## The rankings - **October 2024** — FANZA monthly **#9** - **November 2025** — FANZA monthly **#6** - **H2 2025** — FANZA ranking **#11**, **#5 among freelance performers** ## 2026: the Taiwan award In **March 2026**, at **ADULTOPIA** in Taoyuan, Taiwan, she won **Best Creative Works** for the MAX-A title *Densetsu Beto Chu Jo Kousei to Sensei no Namachūdashi Seikō* — an award for the acting and creative execution of a single work. That a freelance-tier performer's acting was recognised with a named creative prize at an international expo is the point: the volume tier can produce the work that gets awarded. ## Also: mumk and film In **December 2022** she co-founded the four-member idol group **mumk** with [Waka Misono](/blog/misono-waka/). She has acted in the 2025 OP Eiga film *Moso Fanfare* and appeared on radio. ## What this career means **The freelance tier, recognised for its work rather than its volume.** Kashiwagi's career is mostly a ranking story — the volume tier placing consistently — but the ADULTOPIA creative award is the part that matters. It is the industry's international circuit acknowledging a freelance performer's acting as best-in-class, which cuts against the usual reading that the tier is anonymous work. ## Related reading - [JAV actresses: how the career actually works](/blog/jav-actresses-explained/) — the freelance tier - [Waka Misono](/blog/misono-waka/) — the mumk partner and record-breaker - [Ichika Matsumoto](/blog/matsumoto-ichika/) — the freelance-tier record - [How Japan's adult video industry works](/blog/japanese-adult-video-industry/) — SOD and the studio structure **Sources:** [Japanese Wikipedia — 柏木こなつ](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/柏木こなつ).
